valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS (fiscal year ending Jan 2028) viewed at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027), using only information public by the 2026-11-13 close. Anchored on FY2026 guidance of adjusted EPS growth of about flat to +4% from $14.69 ($14.69-$15.28, midpoint about $14.98). Q2 FY2026 (reported 2026-08-18): sales $47.9B, comps +1.7%, adjusted EPS $4.92. Currency USD, US listing, no ADR conversion. The Q3 release of 2026-11-17 is after the reference close and excluded (see analyst_notes).

bear.driver: Housing turnover stays frozen, comps about flat, margin pressure; FY2027 EPS roughly equal to the low end of FY2026 guidance

base.driver: Low-single-digit comps, Pro/SRS growth and buybacks give about 5-6% EPS growth on the FY2026 guidance midpoint

bull.driver: Lower mortgage rates lift housing turnover, comps +3-4%, operating leverage returns

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $15.80 the close implies 22.1x; the analyst-weighted target of about $395 implies 25.0x on base EPS, or about $17.2 EPS at 23x
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $15.80 (4.5 pp of the close)
valuation.watch_metric: US comparable sales growth and operating margin (FY2026 guide: comps flat to +2%, adjusted EPS flat to +4%)
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and fiscal 2026 results, expected February 2027

analyst_notes: Named calls are clustered around the Aug 18-19 Q2 release, with later JPMorgan (raise to $400 from $396 on Nov 9), Melius ($397, Oct 6) and a UBS Buy reaffirmation; no named target cut was verified before the close. Targets of $373-$425 sit 7-22% above the close versus the 4% base case, a gap of roughly 2 P/E turns (25x vs 23x) or about $1.4 EPS. Seven of ten events predate the Nov 17 Q3 release, which is after the reference close and is not used. Published consensus (MarketBeat, 32-33 analysts) is about $371-375 with 18-20 Buy, 12-13 Hold and 1 Sell; Bernstein (Market Perform) and Stifel (Hold) were reported lower but could not be verified, so the sample leans bullish.
